facts.fact: PRODIGY's stakeholder plan reports public consultations of 14 to 25 June 2019 in rural communes of Atsimo Andrefana, Haute Matsiatra, Amoron'i Mania and Vakinankaratra (91 participants, 31 women) at which commune staff reported lacking computers, some civil status secretaries having no computer skills and communes without electricity, and asked whether the paper registers, some in very bad condition, would disappear or stay in use; the document does not itself state in terms that offices register on paper only.

PRODIGY's stakeholder plan of June 2020 states that the Government initiated PRODIGY with the World Bank, listed for financing and technical support, to redefine the civil status and civil identification management systems; consulted communes said they could not bear the running costs of the equipment (internet, backups, ink, antivirus, upkeep).

facts.fact: PRODIGY's stakeholder plan of June 2020 gives the communes the material registration of civil status events and the Ministère de l'Intérieur et de la Décentralisation the management of the national civil status centre, with the Ministry of Justice controlling the registers.
